title: Twenty Minutes of Nothing
subtitle: 休息休闲 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 休息休闲（生活与学习·休息与休闲）
meta: 主题语境：休息休闲（生活与学习·休息与休闲）　|　核心词汇：moment　|　正文 398 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 moment 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Moment, she would have said, is the smallest unit anybody can defend. My grandmother's idea of a holiday was twenty minutes in a chair, and she defended it like a trade. Not a ① moment longer, she said, and not a minute less, because less is not rest and more is not either. She had raised four children and run a shop, and the ② moment she sat down the shop, by her account, carried on without her.

I was sent to stay with her every summer and instructed, by my mother, to keep her company. This was a misunderstanding. Company was not what she wanted; what she wanted was for the house to be quiet at the right ③ moment, which is not the same thing. She timed it. Twenty minutes, and ④ the moment the clock reached the half hour she stood up, however interesting the conversation had become.

I asked her once what she did during it. 'Nothing,' she said, and then, because I was eleven and did not believe her, she explained. A moment, she said, is not a thing you find but a thing you keep: the ⑤ moment of rest is not the absence of work, it is the presence of a rule. A chair at four o'clock is a rule. A chair whenever you collapse is not, and it does not ⑥ momentarily restore anything, because it has no shape.

Every moment in that house had an owner, and most of them were hers. She was not alone in this and she was not unusual. The men on the building site across the road sat down at ten and stood up at twenty past, and if you passed at the wrong time they would tell you so. ⑦ At the moment the site is flats, and most of the men are dead. Rest, I have since noticed, is ⑧ of moment in a way that leisure never is: it is scheduled, it is short, and it is defended.

She died in 2004, at ninety-one, twenty minutes before the hour. I have a chair now and a rule, and I keep it badly. ⑨ The moment I sit down, my phone tells me what somebody wants, and twenty minutes becomes eleven. ⑩ For the moment, at least, I have kept the clock: at half past four, whatever is happening, the chair is not negotiable, and I have never once regretted it afterwards.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 片刻；瞬间；一会儿
B. n. 时刻；时候；关头（某一时间点）
C. conj. 用法：the moment (that) 一……就……
D. adv. 短暂地；片刻地（momentarily）
E. 固定搭配：of moment 重要的；有分量的
F. 固定搭配：for the moment 暂时；目前
G. 固定搭配：at the moment 此刻；目前
H. n. 时机；合适的时刻

items.q: the moment she sat down the shop, by her account, carried on
for the house to be quiet at the right moment
the moment the clock reached the half hour she stood up
the moment of rest is not the absence of work
it does not momentarily restore anything
At the moment the site is flats
Rest, I have since noticed, is of moment
The moment I sit down, my phone tells me
For the moment, at least, I have kept the clock

answers.why: a moment longer 意为“多一刻、再一会儿”，说她不许自己多坐一会儿。
the moment (that) 作连词，意为“一……就……”，说她一坐下，铺子照她说法就自己转了。
at the right moment 意为“在合适的时机”，说屋子该在恰当的时候安静下来。
同样作连词，说钟一走到半点她就站起来。
the moment of rest 意为“休息的时刻”，说休息的时刻不等于没有工作。
momentarily 作副词，意为“片刻地、短暂地”，说随时瘫坐的椅子恢复不了什么。
at the moment 意为“此刻、目前”，说如今那块工地已变成公寓。
of moment 意为“重要的、有分量的”，说休息是件要紧事，而消遣从来不是。
同样作连词，说我一坐下手机就告诉我有人找我。
for the moment 意为“暂时、目前”，说至少目前我还守着那只钟。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 她不许自己多坐一刻，也不许少坐一分钟。（a moment longer）
她一坐下，铺子照她的说法就自己转起来了。（the moment）
钟一走到半点，她就站了起来。（the moment）
休息的时刻不等于没有工作，而是有一条规矩在。（the moment of）
随时瘫倒的椅子片刻也恢复不了什么。（momentarily）
至少目前，我还守着那只钟。（for the moment）
answers: She would not sit a moment longer, and not a minute less.
The moment she sat down, the shop carried on without her.
The moment the clock reached the half hour, she stood up.
The moment of rest is not the absence of work but the presence of a rule.
A chair you collapse into restores nothing, not even momentarily.
For the moment, at least, I have kept the clock.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 moment 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: My grandmother's idea of a holiday was twenty minutes in a chair: not a moment longer, and not a minute less.
The moment she sat down, the shop, by her account, carried on without her.
What she wanted was for the house to be quiet for a moment with a beginning and an end.
The moment the clock reached the half hour she stood up, and she timed it.
Rest, I have noticed, is of moment in a way that leisure never is: it is scheduled, short and defended.
The moment I sit down my phone tells me what somebody wants, but for the moment I have kept the clock.
